title: 5 Common NAATI CCL Mistakes That Cost You Points
excerpt: Interpreting candidates lose marks in the same five places every sitting. Here is what they are, and how to fix each one before your test date.
content:
After scoring thousands of NAATI CCL mock dialogues, our tutors see the same five mistakes repeat themselves. Fix these and your points are close.

1. Register. Most students render everything into the second person. In the CCL test you interpret in the same register the speaker used, and the marker penalises you when you flatten 'would you be able to' into 'can you'.

2. Numbers, dates and names. These are marked on accuracy, not impression. Practise a mental drill: every time you hear a number, repeat it back to yourself in the target language before the dialogue moves on.

3. Idioms rendered literally. 'Behind the eight ball' is not 'behind the eight ball'. Build a bank of the 100 most common English idioms with natural equivalents in your language.

4. Unfinished repairs. Candidates restart sentences mid-way and leave both versions hanging. If you stumble, finish the first attempt, pause, and only then give the corrected version.

5. Silence. Gaps of more than two seconds signal a loss of flow. Learn the filler-free strategy: interpret the last completed clause, then keep the next one ready while you listen.

Mock tests with a certified interpreter will catch all five long before the real sitting. Run one dialogue every second day for a month and your score will move more than a month of passive study.
